We fine-tune ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} on this constructed dataset using standard cross-entropy loss. While we acknowledge a theoretical discrepancy between this training setup (where tokens subsequent to the control command are from model itself) and the inference phase (where tokens are generated by ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} ), this supervised warm-up is essential. It focuses primarily on adapting the model to output valid executable commands ( 𝒞 cmd \mathcal{C}_{\text{cmd}} ). This creates a stable starting point for the subsequent reinforcement learning stage, where ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} will be trained to request token-level assistance from ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} and take advantage of their feedback. In this stage, we employ Reinforcement Learning to align the model’s behavior with our core objective: maximizing response quality while strictly minimizing collaborative cost. We proceed by detailing our optimization framework. We leverage Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al. , 2024 ) to refine the policy π θ \pi_{\theta} of ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} by adopting the Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) paradigm (Lambert et al. , 2024 ) . This paradigm is well-suited for domains where the quality of generated responses can be deterministically verified.
